answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a knoll of collateral to validate network state. If an agent acts maliciously, the protocol cuts its falcon-like speed of influence, resulting in a slashing of assets. By imposing a financial horizon on prospective attackers, this mechanism forces the cost of identity proliferation to scale linearly with capital, making the maintenance of fake identities economically irrational compared to honest participation.
